findings.claim: new_case resolves the case root before calling sync_folder, and the Dropbox info.json roots and OneDrive env roots are never resolved (store.py:195-196). If one of those configured roots runs through a symlink, a resolved root inside it does not match, and its resolved name may not be a client name. So the sync_folder docstring's 'a symlink is followed' covers only a symlinked case root, not a symlinked sync root.
findings.repro: On Linux, make ~/Dropbox a symlink to /data/dbx, have ~/.dropbox/info.json name {"personal":{"path":"/home/ann/Dropbox"}}, and set CMA_HOME=~/Dropbox/cma. firm.case_root() returns /data/dbx/cma. _within(/data/dbx/cma, /home/ann/Dropbox) is False, and no part of /data/dbx/cma is a client name, so `cma case new` makes the case with no warning and no sync_folder_warning entry.

findings.claim: _dropbox_roots catches only OSError and ValueError. A deeply nested info.json raises RecursionError from json.loads, which then escapes `cma case new` as a raw error, though the comment says an unreadable file 'names nothing'. Path.home() (store.py:188) is also unguarded and raises RuntimeError when HOME is unset and there is no passwd entry.
findings.repro: Write ~/.dropbox/info.json as '[' * 100000 + ']' * 100000, then run `cma case new`. json.loads raises RecursionError, which is not caught at store.py:165-166, so the command fails instead of creating the case.

findings.claim: claim.json is inaccurate in places. files_changed lists only README.md and tests/test_sync_folder.py, but the diff also changes src/cma/store.py and src/cma/cli.py. Note (5) says ensure_root makes the root and cases/ before the warning, but commit 1304c14 changed that and the code now warns first (store.py:451-463). The 0.17 ms performance claim comes from an ad-hoc command that the runner did not run, so it is unproven.
findings.repro: Compare claim.json files_changed and notes with `git diff e7c6b17 --stat` and store.py:451-463. No runner tier log contains the perf_counter command.

findings.claim: Detection goes by folder name only, so a folder that a client syncs in place under an ordinary name is missed. The tests even fix one such path as not synced: /Users/ann/Documents/cases (NOT_SYNCED). On macOS, iCloud Drive's 'Desktop & Documents Folders' option syncs ~/Documents, and the default case root is cwd/private/cma. The README's known limits cover this only as 'a folder synced under any other name'.
findings.repro: On a Mac with iCloud Desktop & Documents turned on, run `cma case new` from ~/Documents/project with CMA_HOME unset. The root /Users/<u>/Documents/project/private/cma contains no client name, so there is no warning and no log entry, yet iCloud uploads the case.
